approach: Extend the published genus-7 gonality stratification / CKgP argument (SRC-0002, Sec. 5; Table 1 has c(7)=3) from n<=3 to the missing pointed base case M_7,4 needed for the degree-16 pure-weight induction. Filter M_7,4 by gonality M2 subset M3 subset M4 subset M5=M_7,4. Reuse hyperelliptic/trigonal CKgP for n<=14, Mukai pentagonal CKgP already stated for n<=4, and the general Hf tetragonal bound for the F=(5,5) stratum (n<=7). Isolate the sole new obstruction in the Casnati–Ekedahl F=(4,6) tetragonal strata, where the evaluation bound of SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 becomes equality at n=4, and analyse the residual divisor locus where evaluation can fail.
assumptions: Rational coefficients Q throughout; stacks over C (or char 0) as in SRC-0002/0004.
Published CKgP ranges: c(g) as in SRC-0002 Table 1, in particular c(7)=3 and M^3_{7,n} CKgP for n<=14 (SRC-0004 Lemma 9.9).
Casnati–Ekedahl structure and the genus-7 allowed splitting list of SRC-0005 Sec. 4.4 / SRC-0002 Sec. 5.2.
Mukai equivalence for pentagonal genus-7 curves and its pointed extension SRC-0002 Lemma 5.13 for n<=4.

On a general F=(4,6) tetragonal genus-7 curve, |2D| is complete of dimension 2 (h^0(2D)=3); this is used to get h^0(K-2D)=1 and is standard for a complete basepoint-free g^1_4 but is not re-proved here for every CE splitting stratum.
Prop. 4.2 CKgP permanence (opens, finite stratifications, affine and Grassmann bundles, proper surjective DM maps) as recorded in SRC-0002.
claims: CLAIM A (scope of base case; established reduction). For the degree-16 low-homology induction via the boundary right-exact sequence (SRC-0002 eq. (6.1); packet THM-0003/0004), an open pure-weight input is required whenever n=0,1 and 16>=2g, or n>=2 and 16>=2g-2+n. For (g,n)=(7,4) one has 2g-2+n=16, so W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_7,4;Q) is a required base case among the RED-0001 list.

CLAIM B (what CKgP buys for pure Tate; not tautological generation). By SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3, if a smooth open substack X of a smooth proper DM stack has the CKgP, then cl: A_*(X)_Q -> ⊕_k W_k H^k(X;Q) is surjective. In particular every pure-weight summand W_k H^k(X) is algebraic and pure Hodge–Tate. For even k=16 this yields that W_16 H^{16}(M_7,4) (equivalently the dual pure piece W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}) is a direct sum of Tate twists Q(-8), without needing A^*=R*. (GAP: this is strictly weaker than the published Prop. 4.5 equality W=RH, which also needs A^*=R*.)

CLAIM C (gonality filtration). Maximal gonality on genus 7 is 5. By SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(3), CKgP of each locally closed gonality stratum M^k_{7,4}\M^{k-1}_{7,4} implies CKgP of M_7,4. Strategy: treat k=2,3 (hyperelliptic/trigonal), k=4 (tetragonal via H_{4,7,4}), k=5 (pentagonal via Mukai).

CLAIM D (hyperelliptic/trigonal; no new gap). By SRC-0004 Lemma 9.9 / SRC-0002 Sec. 5.1, for n<=14 the locus M^3_{7,n} has the CKgP and all classes supported on it are tautological. Since 4<=14, M^3_{7,4} is covered by the published range.

CLAIM E (pentagonal; already covers n=4). SRC-0002 Lemma 5.13 embeds the exact-gonality-5 locus M^circ_{7,n} as an open in a Grassmann bundle Gr(7-n,Q_n) over an open in OG(5,V)^n for all n<=4, and concludes CKgP. The independence of spinor images of the n markings uses the absence of a g^1_n on pentagonal genus-7 curves for n<=4, which still applies at n=4. Lemmas 5.14–5.17 further show the Chow ring of M^circ_{7,n} is generated by tautological classes for these n. Thus the pentagonal stratum of M_7,4 is already settled in the literature.

CLAIM F (tetragonal setup). The forgetful map beta'_n: H^♢_{4,7,n} := H_{4,7,n}\beta_n^{-1}(M^3_{7,n}) -> M^4_{7,n}\M^3_{7,n} is proper with the stated image. Prop. 4.2(2) reduces CKgP of the exact tetragonal locus to CKgP of H^♢_{4,7,4}. Stratify by Casnati–Ekedahl splitting types as in SRC-0002 Sec. 5.2 / SRC-0005 Sec. 4.4: X_n = {E=(3,3,4), F=(5,5) or (4,6)}, Y_n = Σ_{2,n} ⊔ Σ_{3,n} with F=(4,6) and E=(2,4,4) or (2,3,5), and Z_n the hyperelliptic maximally unbalanced locus (image inside M^3, already handled).

CLAIM G (F=(5,5) part of X_4; OK). SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 guarantees surjectivity of the evaluation H^0(PE^∨,W)->H^0(Γ,W|Γ) whenever n <= 4f_1-2g+1. For F=(5,5) one has f_1=5, g=7, so the bound is n<=7. Hence for n=4 the F=(5,5) open of X_4 sits in the vector-bundle/open-tower (10.10) of SRC-0004 over a CKgP base B, and Lemmas 10.11–10.12 give CKgP and A^*((PE^∨)^4) surjecting onto that open. No new gap.

CLAIM H (precise F=(4,6) evaluation defect at n=4). For F=(4,6) one has f_2=6. The degree computation in the proof of Lemma 10.6 yields deg(ω_C ⊗ W_{f_2}^∨(Γ)) = 4f_2+n-2g-14. Substituting (g,n,f_2)=(7,4,6) gives degree 0, so the strict inequality 0>deg used to force H^1(C,W(-Γ))=0 becomes equality. Serre duality then says evaluation fails if and only if ω_C ⊗ W_{f_2}^∨(Γ) ≅ O_C has a section. Using O_{PE}(1)|_C ≅ ω_C ⊗ γ^*O_{P^1}(2) for the degree-4 cover γ: C->P^1 with fibre class D, one obtains the identification ω_C ⊗ W_{f_2}^∨(Γ) ≅ ω_C^{-1}(2D+Γ). Thus evaluation fails iff Γ ~ K_C-2D.

CLAIM I (geometry of the residual locus; partial). On a smooth irreducible non-trigonal tetragonal genus-7 curve with a basepoint-free g^1_4 giving D, the complete linear system |2D| is the pullback of |O_{P^1}(2)|, so h^0(2D)=3. Riemann–Roch then gives h^0(K_C-2D)=h^0(2D)-2=1, hence a unique effective residual divisor R~K_C-2D of degree 4. Therefore, over the open of F=(4,6) covers for which R has four distinct points, the bad locus Bad ⊂ H^♢_{4,7,4} of non-surjective evaluation is a degree-24 (=4!) finite étale cover of that unpointed open (orderings of R). Over the closed locus where R has multiple points, Bad is of strictly smaller dimension.

CLAIM J (CKgP on the evaluation-surjective open). Let U_4 ⊂ (PE^∨|_{B_{e,f}})^4 be the open where evaluation (5.4)/(10.9) is surjective, and let H^{good} be the preimage in the F=(4,6) part of H^♢_{4,7,4}. The same tower as in SRC-0002 Lemma 5.3 / SRC-0004 (10.10) realises H^{good} by open inclusions, vector bundles, and projective bundles over a classifying stack B_{e,f} that has the CKgP (affine bundle over products of BGL). Prop. 4.2(1)(4)(5) therefore yields CKgP of H^{good}, and the restriction A^*((PE^∨)^4)->A^*(H^{good}) is surjective.

CLAIM K (intended attack on Bad; incomplete). To upgrade Claim J to CKgP of the full F=(4,6) tetragonal locus one must show CKgP of Bad and apply Prop. 4.2(3). On the open Bad^0 where R is four distinct points, Bad^0 is finite étale over an open of the unpointed stratum Σ_ℓ, and Σ_ℓ itself has the CKgP by the unpointed quotient presentation Σ_ℓ=[(U×G_m)/SL_2 ⋉(Aut E×Aut F)] of SRC-0005 Lemma 3.10 / SRC-0002 p.16. However SRC-0004 Lemma 3.10 only transports CKgP along proper surjections in the domain-to-target direction (if Y has CKgP and Y->X is proper surjective DM-representable then X has CKgP). It does not automatically give CKgP of a finite étale cover of a CKgP base. A direct quotient-stack presentation of Bad^0 (residual points as part of the CE data), or an identification of Bad^0 with an open in a tower of affine/projective bundles over a known CKgP stack, is missing. The multiple-point residual locus is likewise uncontrolled.

CLAIM L (consequence if CKgP of M_7,4 were obtained). Combining Claims D–G and a completed Claim K would give CKgP of every gonality stratum of M_7,4, hence CKgP of M_7,4 by Prop. 4.2(3). Lemma 4.3 would then imply that W_{16} H^{16}(M_7,4;Q) is pure Hodge–Tate algebraic, i.e. a sum of Q(-8). Together with the boundary induction of SRC-0002 (6.1) and the other RED-0001 base cases, this would discharge the pure-Tate (not necessarily tautological) contribution of (g,n)=(7,4) to CONJ-0001 at degree 16. This attempt does NOT obtain that conclusion.

CLAIM M (explicit non-claims). This attempt does not prove CKgP of M_7,4; does not prove A^*(M_7,4)=R^*(M_7,4); does not compute dim W_{-16} H^{BM}_{16}(M_7,4); does not invoke point counts, semisimplifications of Galois representations, or a perfectness statement for a tautological pairing; and does not resolve the other RED-0001 cases (M_3,12), (M_5,8), (M_6,6), (M_8,n) for n=0,1,2.
gap_markers: GAP-1 (main obstruction). CKgP of the residual evaluation-failure locus Bad ⊂ {F=(4,6)} ∩ H^♢_{4,7,4} is not established. Finite étaleness of Bad^0 over the unpointed CE stratum does not, by the published permanence lemmas alone, imply CKgP of Bad^0.
GAP-2. No quotient-stack / bundle-tower presentation of Bad (or of its image in M_7,4) is supplied, so Prop. 4.2 cannot be applied directly to Bad.
GAP-3. Multiple-point residual divisors (R non-reduced or <4 support points) form a closed subset of Bad whose CKgP and contribution to pure weight 16 are not analysed.

GAP-4. Even after CKgP of M_7,4, the equality W_k H^k = RH^k (SRC-0002 Prop. 4.5) requires A^*=R* on M_7,4. The n=4 extension of Lemmas 5.5–5.7 (surjectivity A^*((PE^∨)^n)->A^*(H^♢) and tautological pushforwards) is not completed on Bad; only the weaker pure-Tate consequence of Lemma 4.3 is in scope.

GAP-5. The identification ω⊗W_{f_2}^∨(Γ) ≅ ω^{-1}(2D+Γ) uses the standard CE restriction O_{PE}(1)|_C ≅ ω_C⊗γ^*O(2); a fully expanded line-by-line check for both E-splitting types (2,4,4) and (2,3,5) inside Y_4 and for the F=(4,6) component of X_4 is not written out.
GAP-6. This attempt treats only (g,n)=(7,4). Discharge of RED-0001 / CONJ-0001 still requires independent treatment of M_3,12, M_5,8, M_6,6, and M_8,n (n=0,1,2).

GAP-7. No claim is made that an extension of pure Tate by pure Tate along (6.1) has been checked against weight filtrations for every boundary stratum at degree 16 beyond the published k<=14 pattern; the present note only isolates the open pure-weight input at (7,4).
